title: Self-Authoring Process / Self-Authoring Future Visioning
opening: Compare a future you want with past attempts and the daily life it would require. Keep desired outcomes, assumed routes and observed conditions separate.

labels.comparison: A future title and the life behind it
labels.comparisonIntro: Hypothetical example: a person wants a life of independent inquiry and assumes a particular income arrangement. If that arrangement uses the time, resources or relationships needed for inquiry, test the assumption before treating the route as necessary.
labels.adherenceText: Independent inquiry is the desired outcome. A title or vivid story does not establish the time, resources or relationships needed to live it.
labels.valueText: If a past attempt lost inquiry time to paid work, compare that account with the hours, resources and relationships available now. Treat it as a condition to check, not proof that the desired future is impossible.
labels.outcomeText: Compare a smaller paid-work commitment or a different income arrangement. Check actual costs and protect one inquiry period; revise the route when the facts change.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmTitle: Use only the reflection that helps this choice
labels.rhythmText: The manuscript adapts Self-Authoring from Jordan Peterson and colleagues. This lesson uses that limited reflection; it does not reproduce or validate the whole external program. A possible future is neither a prediction nor a binding identity. A narrow present decision may need only a small reflection, not a whole-life autobiography.
labels.practice: Connect one desired outcome with daily conditions
labels.practiceIntro: Use only the fields that clarify your question. A partial private note is fine; observations, assumptions and desired outcomes need not be complete before you can keep them.
labels.private: This optional private reflection is separate from the six required assessment questions.
labels.length: This full reflection is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote:
Self-Authoring Process / Self-Authoring Future Visioning

or obstructed them, present alignment and a possible future across life domains.
Extract the few outcomes that matter most.

fields.label: A past goal or attempt worth examining

example.qualities: I tried to write regularly while taking extra paid work.
example.contribution: Spend time on independent inquiry that can help people learn.
example.avoid: Extra work occupied the mornings I had intended to use for inquiry.
example.present: I currently need reliable income and have two free mornings each month.
example.connection: The first plan assumes a prestigious research role is essential. A smaller protected inquiry period may also serve the desired life.
example.change: Check the actual income requirement and protect one morning for an inquiry session before choosing a larger commitment.
